terms.grammar: impersonal: dēsinit with the infinitive pluere; perfect dēsiit pluere, it has stopped raining
terms.comment: Cato’s plain words: the verb of stopping with the impersonal pluere. Of the sky clearing afterwards, see “clear up” (disserēnat).

phrases.english: It’s stopped raining; come on, let’s go outside!
It hasn’t stopped raining yet; wait a little.

phrases.latin: in vīllā, cum pluet, circumīre oportet, sīcubi perpluat, et signāre carbōne, cum dēsierit pluere, utī tēgula mūtētur
phrases.english: in the farmhouse, when it rains, you should go round to see where the roof lets the rain in, and mark the place with charcoal, so that the tile can be changed when it stops raining

phrases.latin: juvat imbribus āctīs prōgeniem parvam dulcīsque revīsere nīdōs
phrases.english: they are glad, when the rain is over, to see their little ones and their sweet nests again

sources: Lewis & Short: desino · Lewis & Short: pluo
